t.E631.agn: JECFA set a group ADI 'not specified' for inosinic acid and its calcium, disodium and dipotassium salts (last evaluation 1993) and stated that intake from additive use is far below that of natural nucleotides from foods. In JECFA's 1974 evaluation it was reported that intake of large amounts of these compounds in humans may increase blood uric acid levels and urinary uric acid excretion, and that this should be taken into account for people predisposed to gout and for those taking diuretic medicines that reduce uric acid excretion.
t.E631.body: Inosinates occur naturally in all animal and plant tissues; in humans they are converted to uric acid as the end product.
t.E631.eff.0.t: May increase blood uric acid levels and urinary uric acid excretion
t.E631.eff.0.w: People predisposed to gout and those taking diuretic medicines that reduce uric acid excretion
t.E631.eval: May be of animal (meat/fish) or fermentation origin; the source may not be stated.
t.E631.prod: Produced by microbial fermentation or by breaking down RNA obtained from yeast.
t.E631.regx.0: ADI not specified (group ADI for inosinic acid and its salts).
t.E631.regx.1: In the E 626–635 ribonucleotides group; authorised at quantum satis in salt substitutes and seasonings/spice blends.
t.E631.regx.2: Re-evaluation ongoing; a call for data was published in 2023 (deadline 31.03.2024).
t.E631.summary: The sodium salt of inosinic acid; a flavour enhancer from the nucleotide group. Obtained from meat or fish or by fermentation; used together with MSG.
t.E631.what: A flavour enhancer that strengthens meaty (umami) taste in food; a derivative of inosine 5'-monophosphate (IMP).
